_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
LINKED grows when matched TUs become reachable in the port's linked call graph.
Actor methods and free functions both count. Enrollment alone does not increase
the count when the release build still dead-strips the unreachable object.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 97b51649d, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT25: tree clean, reconfigure with the four hostgen register TUs, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10503 with all 51 level and 37 scene rows including the Game Over scene, the six proofs, the loopback pair with the ROM's own wireless worker created, entered, slept and woken on the parent, the four-player proof, the rollback ladder at eight wide with every session row green including seven windows at 160 ms, and a captured level under the ROM's own frame loop), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow on every push of port/** and every pull request into the shipping branch. +106 over the previous stamp of 10397, +470 over the 2026-09-08 morning's 10033, +1382 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. Since the 10397 stamp: the ROM's own wireless worker thread and its session over the hosted ARM7 (+20), the touch panel answered by a hosted ARM7 arm with the console's firmware calibration published (+9), the ROM's own static-initialiser runner at Entry's own instruction (+18), the sound command layer and its frame (+34), the mother penguin's cells and the Game Over scene hosted as ROM bodies (+21), plus zero-gain rungs that make the port more the decomp: four I/O placeholders spelled as the registers they stood for and the ROM's own game loop driving a level frame behind a knob, a decomp function's forgotten register-borne arguments restored byte for byte, the four-player re-seat and the ROM's five-second drop bound honoured. Running: the ROM's loop as the default frame driver (the flip), the ROM's own touch-ring writer, the remaining register-borne signatures on the decomp side.
